title: UNM Health ransomware attack disrupts patient care, surgeries
content_md: The University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center disclosed a cyberattack that caused system outages and disrupted patient care and academic activities. On Monday, UNM Health, the university’s healthcare provider, began temporarily limiting new patient admissions, diverting ambulances to nearby hospitals, and suspending outpatient surgeries and appointments. In an update on the incident, UNM said UNM Hospital and Sandoval Regional Medical Center remain open, and all clinics will resume scheduled appointments and procedures starting today, Tuesday, October 27. Regarding emergencies, the healthcare organization advised that people should call 911. However, today’s classes at its four health sciences schools are canceled, and nonessential HSC employees were instructed to stay home. UNM Health is a major statewide provider of specialist care with more than 1 million patient visits annually. Its flagship UNM Hospital in Albuquerque houses New Mexico’s only Level I trauma center , treating the most seriously injured patients. UNM did not disclose the type of cyberattack it suffered, but BleepingComputer found that a new ransomware group called Byod had claimed the attack. In a post on their data leak site, the threat actor said it had compromised 36,000 systems across UNM’s main campus and hospital environments, including Active Directory forests, Group Policy infrastructure, the entire Microsoft Entra tenant, and two Oracle databases.
